title: How can I create a pipeline so that multiple agents work together?
author: pixelmarbles
selftext:
I currently use Codex. I want to form a team of agents, each has their own role. For example, 

* Agent A does the game design
* Agent B does architecture and code design
* Agent C does the coding

I give an idea to Agent A, Agent A creates the GDD, the GDD will be read by Agent B and will create an architecture/code design document, that document will be read by Agent C and starts coding. When it's done, I can playtest the game and provide feedback to Agent A/C.

While I'm not working on my main game (due to my day job), I just wanna test out my ideas and create prototypes using this method.

comments.author: Free_Afternoon_7349
comments.body:
You can have them just write it in .md docs and then tell the other one to read it. 

Personally when I get the AI to 1 shot core architecture of a game - say like rust server + custom ts client - I will usually do it in a single long conversation, first talk about the game, then have the AI do some research, and then I'll have it write a 1 shot doc, and then I will have it implement that. 

Though from that it is a ton of tuning and fixing edge cases and playtesting and such to get something really smooth going

replies.author: Darknessborn
replies.body: As a first step I reckon having the AI interview you in voice mode (acting as a AAA gamer designer) and getting it to build that out into notion. From there it's a 2 agent process and MD files work really well for that

replies.author: pixelmarbles
replies.body: I get this but what I want is for me to not need to manually feed the input into the next agent.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
This sounds like the complete opposite of what you would want to do to get anything useful built.

I’ve been running a trial process with multiple chats, a shared backlog and docs and a very simple gameplay idea. I’ve got skills to support them, an MCP for running the backlog and an LLM wiki for game design references.

I still have to guide and correct all of the way through, and the coding tasks burn through tokens. From simple syntax errors to major architectural short sightedness, the agents are not independent developers.

AI tools should help you to accelerate your project by working in short, clear loops of idea, build, test and learn. If you could somehow build that without the need for much human intervention you’ll be flying, but it won’t be cheap.

replies.author: pixelmarbles
replies.body: Like I mentioned, it's just for prototyping. And besides, I can always intervene when something is not right. And it's not like I'm gonna build something with a really big scope.

comments.body: you're basically describing a spec-driven pipeline where each agent's output feeds the next. CrewAI can do this if you wire it up yourself, but it's a lot of config. Zenflow from zencoder.ai does exactly this with multi-agent orchestration built in.

comments.author: Ohgood9002
comments.body:
Step 1 - Convert all your game documentation into .md files. Put them all in the root folder of your project. This is your game design, your narrative design, your art design, your music design, lore, characters, everything. If you haven't fully developed all those systems then you really need to create baseline documentation before this can work. 

The best way to spec out missing systems is to prompt "Ask me 10-15 questions about \_\_\_\_\_ system. Use my responses to make a design .md for the project.

  
Step 2 - Write a AGENTS.md. This will be where you clearly define the roles each AI agent has, along with instructions for the AI agents to only stick to their roles. I would recommend you ask AI to help you define the roles for each agent and then ask you 10 questions about the project and use those answers to write the AGENTS.md. If you're using Claude and already have a Claude.md file you'll want to update it so it points Claude to the new AGENTS.md

I use two agents. Claude and Codex. Claude designs the car, Codex is the mechanic.



Step 3 - Write an IMPLEMENTATION.md. This is what the agents will use to "talk" to each other. After each change is made to the project the agents will log what was implemented so another agent can pick up where the previous agent left off. Your AGENTS.md that you wrote in step 2 needs to have rules for the AI agents to log what they have implemented after they make any changes or updates to the project. 

I would recommend that you ask AI to write the IMPLEMENTATION.md. Give it a prompt like "I want the AI agents to be able to "talk" to each other. Write an implementation.md that the AI agents can use to stay updated on any project changes. That way they will be able to pick up where the other AI agents left off with clean handoffs"

  
You'll occasionally want to have all 3 agents audit the project and align all documentation to catch any fringe cases. I find that writing your own scaffolding for your project works better than relying on superpowers or skills.

comments.author: Fake_Gbler
comments.body:
if Agent A writes a vague GDD, Agent B will drift, and Agent C will hallucinate even more imo. so the first thing is defining strict formats for each stage (e.g., GDD = sections + bullet specs, architecture doc = systems + APIs + data models, coding = tasks + files + functions). 


in practice, i'd set up smth like - takes input doc -> transforms -> outputs new doc, runs with a narrow prompt + role + constraints, optionally validates the previous step (like Agent B checking if GDD is complete before proceeding). you’ll also want a feedback loop. after playtesting, feed structured feedback back into Agent A or C (“bug list”, “missing features”, “feel issues”) instead of just raw thoughts. otherwise the system drifts over time. versioning helps too (v1 GDD -> v2 updates), so agents aren’t constantly rewriting everything. for gamedev specifically, make sure to prebuilt assets/animation tools to speed up the “playtestable” stage. i personally use reallusion (character creator / iclone / actorcore), it can plug into this kind of pipeline so my coding agent isn’t blocked on creating characters/animations from scratch, it just references existing rigs/assets and focuses on logic.


Hope this helps!
